assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
caveats: Success rate depends on the denominator: attempt-level is 89.2%, order-level 91.6% and technical 92.9%; retries and drop-offs explain the gap.
Duplicate records on 12 Oct (341 attempts ingested twice) were removed, keeping the first ingestion.
The 18-31 Oct volume spike is not a data error by itself, but check it before comparing totals across this period.

facts.text: The attempt-level success rate for 1-31 October 2026 was 89.2%, from 384,193 successful attempts out of 430,580 total attempts.

The order-level success rate was 91.6% (384,192 successful out of 419,385 orders) and the technical success rate was 92.9% (384,193 successful out of 413,684). The widest gap between the three definitions is 3.64pp.
On 12 Oct, 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts); each attempt is counted once in the figures above.
Attempt volume from 18 Oct to 31 Oct was 39% above the usual level for those weekdays, over 14 days.

response.headline: October 2026 attempt success rate was 89.2% (384,193 successful out of 430,580 attempts), counting every retry as its own attempt.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Compare attempts per order and the share of orders that succeeded only after a retry in October.
hypotheses.rationale: Attempt-level counts every retry as a separate attempt, so failed first tries that later succeed pull the attempt rate down, while order-level rates credit the eventual success.
hypotheses.text: The gap between the attempt-level rate (89.2%) and the order-level (91.6%) and technical (92.9%) rates is largely explained by retries and customer drop-offs.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check the sale/campaign calendar and compare order counts and revenue for 18-31 Oct against ingestion logs.
hypotheses.rationale: Real business events and data gaps both produce volume spikes of this kind, and the evidence cannot tell them apart.
hypotheses.text: The 18-31 Oct volume spike may reflect a sale or promotion rather than a data gap.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: The order-level success rate was 91.6% and the technical success rate was 92.9%.
recommendations.rationale: The three definitions differ by up to 3.64pp, so comparing numbers across teams without a shared definition can mislead.
recommendations.text: When reporting October's success rate, state the definition used (attempt-level 89.2%) and show order-level and technical rates alongside.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: The 18-31 Oct volume spike may reflect a sale or promotion rather than a data gap.
recommendations.rationale: A +39% volume change can distort period-over-period comparisons if it is not understood.
recommendations.text: Confirm whether the 18-31 Oct volume spike was a planned sale before comparing October totals with other months.
